key_findings.finding: The most likely diagnosis is glycogen storage disease type I (von Gierke disease), especially GSD Ia from G6PC deficiency (or GSD Ib/SLC37A4 deficiency). The phenotype is classic: profound fasting intolerance/hypoglycemia, growth retardation with preserved weight, doll-like facies, protuberant abdomen, massive hepatomegaly, and hyperlipidemia. GSD-I results from impaired conversion of glucose-6-phosphate to free glucose, blocking both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; excess G6P is diverted to glycogen and lipogenesis, producing hepatomegaly, hypertriglyceridemia/lipemic blood, lactic acidosis, and often hyperuricemia.

source_tools.relevance: Authoritative disease record with definition, clinical manifestations, G6PC/SLC37A4 genes, and mechanism
Case evidence describing doll-like face, protuberant abdomen, massive hepatomegaly, hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, and hyperlipidemia

key_findings.finding: The biochemical/pathophysiologic discriminator is severe fasting hypoglycemia with inability to generate free glucose from glucose-6-phosphate, accompanied by lactic acidemia, hypertriglyceridemia/hypercholesterolemia and commonly hyperuricemia; confirmation is by low G6Pase pathway activity and biallelic G6PC or SLC37A4 variants. This distinguishes the case from congenital hyperinsulinism (inappropriately high insulin/C-peptide and suppressed ketones, without the characteristic massive glycogen/fatty hepatomegaly and lipemia), CPT II deficiency or fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase deficiency (episodic decompensation rather than persistent doll-face hepatomegaly/hyperlipidemia), and the lysosomal/storage or lipid disorders listed (which do not produce this combined fasting-hypoglycemia–hepatomegaly–lipemia pattern; Gaucher and Niemann-Pick A usually involve splenomegaly, while LPL deficiency causes lipemia but not profound fasting hypoglycemia with glycogenotic facies).
